topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and sets out the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causes.

topics.label: Genetic, environmental, and stochastic contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational interplay between acquired genetic mutations, environmental exposures, and stochastic biological processes in determining cancer risk across populations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how infectious pathogens drive malignancy, focusing on oncogenic mechanisms and the specific etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and promotional carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutagens, metabolic activation pathways, host susceptibility, and non-mutagenic tumor promoters induce DNA damage and drive cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro tools used to identify carcinogens and assess the practical risks of exposure.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing summary of the lecture's core themes and final concluding remarks.
